title: Creating a report
intro: A report collects the readings from the sensors you choose and emails them to the people you choose, on a schedule. This guide makes one from start to finish.

content.text: A report gathers up the readings from the sensors you choose over a period of time, and sends the result to the people you choose, on a schedule. Nobody has to remember to do anything.
A rule tells you the moment something goes wrong. A report tells you how things have been. They answer different questions, and most sites end up using both.
This guide is about making and changing a report. What the finished report contains, and how to read it, is a separate guide.
Have these ready:

items.text: The sensors the report should cover.
How often you want it: every week, at the end of each month, or both.
The email address of everybody who should receive it.

content.text: Saving a report also needs two things from your account:

items.text: Manager or above on every sensor in the report
, or being its owner. The sensor list offers every sensor you can see, but saving with one you cannot manage is refused with “You do not have permission to manage one or more selected devices”.
The reporting add-on.

Without it, the Reports page shows a yellow panel headed “Reporting subscription required”, and the button that saves a report stays grey. “Subscribe to reporting” in that panel starts the subscription. Accounts billed by invoice have no button there; ask CropWatch to switch reporting on.

content.text: You can save a report and come back to it later. Nothing is sent until the schedule comes round.

items.text: Sign in and go to
Reports
in the menu. The list is headed
Report Templates
Press the
button above the list, on the right.

content.text: CropWatch calls it a “report template” because it is the recipe, not the finished report. The recipe runs on your schedule and produces a new report each time.

image.alt: The Reports page listing report templates, with the plus button above the list
image.caption: The + button above the list starts a new report.

content.text: The first card is headed “1. Template”.

items.text: Name
— what the people receiving it will see. “Weekly operations summary” is the sort of thing.
Description
— optional notes for your team.
Data pull interval
— how closely the report looks at the data: every 30 minutes, or every hour. Leave it at 30 minutes unless you have a reason. It does not change how often the report is sent.
Active template
— leave it on. Off means the report is kept but never produced, which is how you pause one.

image.alt: Step one of the report form: Name, Description, Data pull interval and the Active template switch
image.caption: The name is what recipients see.

content.text: The second card is headed “2. Device Assignments”. Tick every sensor the report should cover. They are grouped by location, and the box filters as you type.
One report can cover several sensors, and they all appear in the same document. If you would rather each greenhouse had its own report, make one report per greenhouse instead.

image.alt: Step two of the report form, with two sensors ticked under their location
image.caption: Everything you tick ends up in the same report.

content.text: The “Delivery schedule” card decides when a report is produced. It has two switches and a box:

items.text: Weekly
: one report each week. A new report starts with this one switched on.
End of month
: one report at the end of each month.
UTC offset (hours)
: your time zone, as a number of hours. Japan is 9. It starts at 0, and with the wrong number the report's days begin and end at the wrong hour.

content.text: These are switches, not a choice of one. Turning on both gives you a report every week and another at the end of the month. There is no daily report to choose.

At least one of the two must be switched on. If neither is, saving stops and says “Choose at least one cadence (daily, weekly, or monthly) for the active schedule.” The message mentions daily, but only Weekly and End of month can be switched on.

image.alt: The Delivery schedule card with Weekly and End of month switches, Weekly switched on, and a UTC offset box
image.caption: Weekly, with the UTC offset set to 9 for Japan.

content.text: The “Recipients” card is the list of people who get the report. On a new report there is already one recipient: you, with the email address on your CropWatch account. Change it if somebody else should receive this one.
Press the + button at the top right of the card for each further person. Each gets a numbered block, “Recipient 2” and so on, with three boxes:

items.text: Send by
: Email.
Email address
: where it goes.
Name
: who it is, so the list makes sense later.

content.text: Add as many as you need. “Remove” takes one off the list, and appears only when there is more than one, so a report always has somebody to go to.

image.alt: The Recipients card with one recipient: Send by Email, an email address and a name, and a + button for adding another
image.caption: Each recipient needs an address and a name.

sections.heading: Alerts: the part that is easy to miss

content.text: The “Alerts” card looks optional. It is not. A report with nothing in this card is saved happily and then never produces anything, because the alerts are what tell CropWatch which measurement to put in the report.
Press “Add alert” and fill in:

items.text: Name
— what this one means, such as “Too cold”.
Condition
— “Less than (<)”, “Greater than (>)”, “Range” and so on.
Threshold
— the number. A Range asks for a “Minimum” and a “Maximum” instead.
Highlight color
— the colour used to mark those readings in the report.

content.text: In the finished report, each alert does three things:

items.text: Readings past the threshold are shaded in its colour, so problems stand out.
A summary line says how many readings matched, and what share of the period that was.
Those readings are always listed, even if the sampling would have skipped over them.

content.text: Alerts here are about temperature, and they never message anybody — they only colour the report. To be told at the time something happens, make an alert rule instead.

image.alt: The Alerts card with one alert: a name, a condition of Less than, a threshold of 5 and a red highlight colour
image.caption: Without at least one of these, the report is never produced.

sections.heading: The advanced section, and why to leave it alone

content.text: Between the Delivery schedule and the Alerts card is a folded-up panel headed “(ADVANCED) Data Processing Schedules”. It throws away readings outside the hours you name, for example counting only working hours.
Its own warning is worth repeating:
“If you do not know what this is, please reach out to support before adding any settings here. Incorrect schedules can silently remove data from your reports.”
Leave it closed. With nothing in it, every reading in the period is used, which is what almost everybody wants.

image.alt: The advanced Data Processing Schedules panel, showing its warning to contact support first
image.caption: Leave this one closed unless support asks you to open it.

content.text: Press “Create Report Template” at the bottom. A green message confirms it and you land back on the list.

If that button is grey and will not press, something is still missing. Once you start filling in the form, a yellow panel headed “Please check these fields” appears at the top and lists what. The usual ones are:

items.text: “Enter a report name.”
“Select at least one device for this report template.”
“Choose at least one cadence (daily, weekly, or monthly) for the active schedule.”
A recipient with a missing or misspelled email address.

content.text: If the button stays grey and the panel lists nothing, look for the “Reporting subscription required” panel at the top of the page. Without the reporting add-on, no report can be saved.

image.alt: The warning listing what is still missing, with the Cancel and Create Report Template buttons
image.caption: The warning names each thing to fix.

sections.heading: Changing, pausing or deleting a report

content.text: Each row on the Reports page has three buttons on the right:

items.text: The pencil
opens it for changing. The last button then says “Save Changes”.
The clock

opens “View History”: the reports this template has already produced, grouped by sensor, each with a “Download” button. If it says “No reports have been generated yet.”, the first one is still to come.
The bin
deletes the template. It asks first, naming the report: “Are you sure you want to delete the report template "Weekly operations summary"? This cannot be undone.”

content.text: Saving changes and deleting both need Manager or above on every sensor in the report; anyone else gets “You do not have permission to manage one or more selected devices”. Downloading a report only needs access to the sensor.
To stop a report for a while, open it and switch “Active template” off rather than deleting it. Reports already sent are not affected by any of this.

image.alt: A row in the reports list with three buttons: a pencil to change it, a clock to see reports already sent, and a bin to delete it
image.caption: The three buttons on each row of the list.

sections.heading: Adding notes to a report that has already been sent

content.text: Sometimes a reading needs an explanation: the door was open, the heater was being serviced. On air temperature and humidity sensors you can write that onto a report that has already been produced.

items.text: On the Reports page, press the clock button on the row.

Find the report and press “Edit” beside it. The button is there only for sensors where you are Manager or above, or the owner, and it is greyed out once the report's period ended more than 23 months ago.

The “Edit report notes” page lists that period's readings, with a “Notes” column. Press the note button on a row to see its notes, then use “Add note”, “Edit” or “Remove”, and press “Apply”. Each change is marked “unsaved”, and “Restore” brings back a note you removed by mistake.
Press “Save Changes”. “Notes saved. The report will be regenerated on the next scheduled run.” confirms it.

content.text: Back in View History, that report carries a “Regeneration queued · 1 edit(s)” badge until the next run. Leaving the notes page before saving asks “You have unsaved note changes. Leave without saving them?” first.

The report is rebuilt with your notes on the next scheduled run and kept beside the original. It is not emailed to the recipients again, so download it from View History when you need it. Notes added on the sensor's own page appear here too; see
Notes on readings

items.text: No alerts.
The report saves, and then nothing ever arrives. See
Alerts: the part that is easy to miss
The UTC offset left at zero.
It starts at 0. In Japan it should be 9, or the report is cut off at nine in the morning rather than at midnight.
Expecting it straight away.
A report arrives when its schedule comes round, not when you save it.
Confusing the two intervals.
“Data pull interval” is how closely the data is looked at. The Delivery schedule is how often the report is sent.
Opening the advanced panel.
Readings can disappear from the report with no warning.
A sensor that stopped reporting.
The report still arrives; that sensor is simply missing from it.
A grey save button with nothing listed.
The account has no reporting add-on yet. See
Before you start
